driver_box.lead: The driver is the person who follows your project: they validate the analysis and take you through to the demo.

driver_box.ignored_driver: With autonomous work, the project is not attributed to {name}.

not_logged.text: You need to log in to send the request or to see an analysis.

missing.title: Incomplete request
missing.text: The answer to “What do you need?” is missing. Go back and complete it.

invalid.title: Invalid request
invalid.text: The request was not recorded. Reload the pre-analysis and send it again.

too_large.title: Request too long
too_large.text: The request exceeds the maximum length and was not recorded. Shorten your answers and try again.

unavailable.title: Service unreachable
unavailable.text: The request was not recorded because a service is not responding. Try again in a few minutes.

not_found.title: Analysis not found
not_found.text: This analysis does not exist, or it belongs to another account.

underspecified.title: A few more details are needed
underspecified.text: What you wrote does not yet say what the tool should do. Add some detail to the answers below and send the request again: what you had written is still here.

analysis.title: Analysis
analysis.heading: Let us bring the request into focus.
analysis.lead: One question at a time, to fill in what the request does not say yet. Answer in your own words; if you do not know, say so.
analysis.opening: I have read your request. I will ask a few questions to complete it, one at a time.
analysis.label: Your message
analysis.hint: Enter sends the message, Shift+Enter starts a new line.

summary.title: The project
summary.empty: No particular terms: we assign the driver.

turns.label: Turns used
turns.warning: Turns still available: {left} of {max}. Once they are used it will no longer be possible to write on this page: any missing information should be provided now. Additional turns can be purchased afterwards, or the request can proceed with what has been collected.

exhausted.title: No turns left
exhausted.lead: The {max} question-and-answer turns included in the pre-analysis have been used. Additional turns can be purchased in order to continue the conversation.
exhausted.optional: Purchasing is not required: the request can proceed with the information already collected. The “This is fine, let's go!” button is now active.
exhausted.download_hint: Downloading the conversation produces a file with all the information collected so far. The file can be submitted to an external AI assistant — ChatGPT or Claude, for instance — to complete the description without using turns, and uploaded later from the pre-analysis page, in the “Ready-made analysis” box.
exhausted.credit_none: You have no turns in credit.
exhausted.credit_too_many: The number is higher than the available credit.
exhausted.credit_invalid: Say how many turns to add: a whole number, at least 1.

analysis.error: The operation could not be completed. Please try again.

login_done.title: Login
login_done.ok_text: You can close this window and go back to the pre-analysis. If it does not close by itself, go back to the previous window and reload the page.
login_done.failed_text: Login did not succeed. Close this window and try again from the pre-analysis.

problem.hint: This is the part that matters. The rest are details that help us understand it.

skill.legend: What it must be able to do
skill.hint: These are not features of your tool, but capabilities it might need. Tick only the ones you are sure of: the rest comes later.

boundaries.hint: Boundaries help too: saying “I handle payments elsewhere” saves us a round of questions.

need.label: What do you need?
need.hint: Describe it in your own words, the way you would tell a friend. It does not need to be precise.
need.placeholder: Example: I run a small spare-parts warehouse and keep track of everything in a notebook. I would like to know at any time what I have, what is running out and where I put it.

today.label: How do you do it now?

options.spreadsheet: With an Excel or Google Sheets spreadsheet
options.other_software: With software that does not fit
options.none: I don't do it yet: I want to start

pain.label: What wastes most of your time, or makes you make mistakes?
pain.hint: If there is a moment in the week when you think “what a chore”, that is what we want to hear about.

options.few: Me and a few other people (2–5)
options.external: Also outsiders: customers, partners, the public

devices.label: What will you use it on?
devices.hint: More than one answer, if needed.

options.ocr: Read the text in photos and scans
options.barcodes: Read or create barcodes and QR codes
options.import: Read existing Excel or CSV files
options.search: Search freely across all the data
options.dates: Work with dates: deadlines, working days, shifts
options.validations: Check Italian tax codes, VAT numbers, IBANs
options.reminders: Send a reminder by itself when something is due
options.signature: Collect a signature drawn on the screen
options.login: Give everyone their own password, and decide who sees what
options.audit_log: Keep a history of who changed what

skills_other.label: Other
skills_other.hint: Need something that is not on the list? Write it in one short line. Only write it if you are sure: if in doubt, leave it blank and we will talk about it later. This is also the place for things that rely on an external service to set up — payments, WhatsApp, Google — which can be done, but case by case.
skills_other.placeholder: Example: read the temperature from a sensor in a cold room

out_of_scope.label: Is there anything you want to keep out?
out_of_scope.hint: Things you will keep doing elsewhere, parts you are not interested in, or that you have seen go wrong in another project.
out_of_scope.placeholder: Example: my accountant handles payments, they must stay out. And I don't want customers to see purchase prices.

personal_data.label: Will it hold data about other people (names, contacts, health data)?
personal_data.hint: That is not a problem: it only changes how we store it.

options.sensitive: Yes, and some of it is sensitive (health, minors, money)

existing_data.label: Do you already have data to bring in?

out_of_scope.title: We cannot go on with this request
out_of_scope.lead: From what you described, webtools is probably not the right tool for this need.

not_software.title: This is not a request for software
not_software.lead: webtools analyses and builds small software only: tools you use in a browser. It does not produce anything else — a graphic moodboard, texts or translations, or a professional opinion, for example.

not_recognised.title: We did not recognise the request
not_recognised.lead: We are sorry, but the analysis tool cannot make out your request.

index.title: webtools — small tailor-made software tools
index.description: Small digital tools built to measure for precise needs. They open with a link, with nothing to install.

hero.heading: Software for that one thing.
hero.text: A webtool is a small digital tool made to meet one precise need. It opens with a link, runs in the browser and you can use it on a computer, tablet or phone, with nothing to install.

stage.label: Illustrative example of a wine cellar webtool
stage.heading: My bottles

small.heading: Small does not mean generic.
small.text: The point is to build only what is needed. No huge platform to learn, no package full of features that will never be switched on.

league.title: League table for a tournament
league.text: Teams, results and standings updated according to the rules of your tournament.

tools.title: Tool inventory
tools.text: A simple map of what there is, where it is and what is missing.

docs.title: Document sorting
docs.text: You upload files, sort them with your own rules and find them again without digging through endless folders.

value.text: One job, one result. Once you accept the demo you receive the complete software, the source code and the ZIP with the instructions. There is no recurring fee to keep paying.

what.title: What a webtool is
what.description: A small, focused digital tool, built for a precise need and usable straight from the browser.
what.heading: A small, focused tool of your own.
what.lead: A webtool is made to do one precise thing well. You open it with a link, use it in the browser and there is nothing to install on the device.

not_an_app.heading: It is not an app to look for in a store.
not_an_app.text1: It is small software reached over the web. That lets it work on computers, tablets and phones without shipping different versions.
not_an_app.text2: It can store data, apply rules, do calculations, organise information or make a repetitive task simpler.

points.need: It is built around a defined need.
points.source: On delivery you also receive the source code.

scale.heading: The right scale matters.
scale.text: A webtool makes sense when the problem is too specific to be solved well by a generic product, but narrow enough not to need a large software project.

need.title: A precise need
need.text: For example: keeping an archive, applying a few rules, collecting availability, logging maintenance.

scope.title: A clear scope
scope.text: What the tool must do is decided first. That is the boundary of the work and also the criterion it is judged by.

no_platform.title: No giant platform
no_platform.text: It is not a universal management system and does not try to replace an entire software ecosystem.

practice.label: in practice
practice.text: The technology stays in the background. You do not need to know frameworks, servers or architectures to use it: you need to know what the tool must do.

spec.title: Write the specification
spec.text: It describes concretely what the webtool must do. You can prepare it with a guided prompt to use with the AI of your choice.

review.title: The specification is reviewed
review.text: We check that the work suits this format and that the scope is clear enough. There is no long cycle of clarifications.

accept.title: You accept the specification
accept.text: If the proposal is acceptable, the specification is marked as final. From then on it is the reference for development and for checking the result.

develop.title: The webtool is developed
develop.text: You do not have to follow the work step by step. The next time you step in is the demo.

demo.title: You see the demo
demo.text: The demo does not open a round of revisions. It is where you choose whether to accept or reject the webtool as it was developed against the specification.
demo.no: You reject → the process ends, with no payment

pay.title: You pay only after accepting
pay.text: If you accept the demo, you pay the agreed price. The standard price of a webtool is {price}.

zip.title: You receive the ZIP
zip.text: The delivery includes the complete software, the source code and the installation instructions.

after.title: After delivery
after.text: If the software does not match the accepted specification, the work needed to make it compliant is free. New features or changes of mind belong to a new job instead.

how.title: How it works
how.description: From the specification to the demo, through to the delivery of the software and its source code.
how.heading: First we decide what it must do. Then we build it.
how.lead: The path is short and clearly bounded. The specification defines the work; the demo is where you decide whether to accept the result.

contacts.title: Contacts
contacts.description: Direct contact for information about the webtools service.
contacts.heading: An email is enough.

panel.title: Direct contact
panel.text: This page will stay deliberately simple: an email address and only the operational information needed.
panel.placeholder: Email address to be added before publication
panel.placeholder_note: The specification gives no real address, so none is made up here.

examples.title: Webtool examples
examples.description: Concrete examples of small tailor-made digital tools: archives, league tables, logs, quotes, shifts and more.
examples.heading: The scale is easier to grasp by looking at it.
examples.lead: These are examples of the kind of tools that can be built. They are not ready-made products to pick from: each webtool comes from a specific need.

cellar.title: Wine cellar archive
cellar.text: Bottles, vintages, shelves and tasting notes in an archive made for your own collection.

league.text: Enter the results and get the standings according to the rules you set.
league.head: Tournament

library.title: Book or record archive
library.text: A personal collection with fields and filters chosen around how you really use it.
library.head: Shelf

garage.title: Car or motorbike maintenance log
garage.text: Deadlines, repairs, mileage and documents without turning it all into a management system.
garage.head: Garage

quote.title: Quote calculator with a few specific rules
quote.text: A calculation that today lives in a spreadsheet, a table or in the head of whoever prepares the quotes.
quote.head: Quote

shifts.title: Shifts and availability
shifts.text: A small group says when they are available. The coordinator sees the whole picture without chasing messages.
shifts.head: Availability

inventory.title: Tool or material inventory
inventory.text: What there is, how much of it and where it is. With the categories that workshop needs.
inventory.head: Storeroom

garden.title: Vegetable garden diary
garden.text: Sowing, transplanting, harvests and notes tied to your plots, not to a generic farming model.
garden.head: Garden

docs.title: Document classification
docs.text: A small queue of files to assign to categories, cases or destinations defined by your workflow.
docs.head: Documents

work_with_us.title: Work with us
work_with_us.description: Working with webtools: ambassador, driver, autonomous work.
work_with_us.heading: Three ways to work with webtools.
work_with_us.lead: All three start with signing up as a driver, our collaborator.

ambassador.title: Become an ambassador
ambassador.text1: Once you have signed up as a driver, you can invite other people to use webtools.
ambassador.text2: If the project of someone you invited succeeds, that is, the client accepts the demo and pays, 50% of the system fee goes to you.
ambassador.text3: To invite someone, you generate a link from your driver area and send it to them.

driver.title: Driver
driver.text1: The driver follows clients’ projects: they validate the analysis and take the clients through to the demo. Most of the earnings per project go to you; the system keeps a small fee.
driver.text2: When you sign up you can ask to become an enabled driver. We hold an interview and, if it goes well, you can follow the projects you bring in or those the system assigns to you.
driver.text3: From then on you can generate your personal links: whoever arrives through one of your links has you as their driver. You can even decide to give small discounts to your clients.

autonomous.title: Autonomous work
autonomous.text1: As a driver (enabled or not) you can use webtools for your own projects and pay per use with your tokens, plus the system fee.
autonomous.text2: Tokens are the credit of your driver account, and you use them precisely for autonomous work. At each step (pre-analysis, analysis, development) the system deducts the tokens consumed.
autonomous.text3: The code is yours: you can use it, resell it or do whatever you like with it. If you wish, you can also delete the code from our system: that gives you semi-deterministic certainty that the code is unique.
autonomous.note: If your tokens run out, the system warns you by email. After topping up you can unblock the stalled pipelines.

recurring.question: Are there recurring costs?
recurring.answer: Not for the webtool itself. There may be external costs, for example a VPS, a domain or third-party services it needs to run.

source.question: Do I really get the source code?
source.answer: Yes. The complete source code is part of the delivery, together with the software and the instructions.

others.question: Can I have someone else modify it?
others.answer: Yes. The delivered software is at your disposal and you can have it modified by whoever you like.

compliance.question: What happens if, after delivery, something does not match the specification?
compliance.answer: The work needed to bring the software back in line with the accepted specification is free.

new_feature.question: And if I want to add a new feature?
new_feature.answer: A new feature or a change of mind is not a compliance fix. The delivered work does not evolve within the same job.

hosting.question: Is hosting included?
hosting.answer: No. VPS, domain and other external infrastructure costs are not included in the standard price.

yours.title: The software is yours
yours.text: You can use it, modify it, have it modified, reuse it and dispose of it freely.

no_fee.title: No recurring fee
no_fee.text: No ongoing support is sold and there is no subscription tied to the webtool.

not_exclusive.title: The code is not exclusive
not_exclusive.text: Delivery gives you full use of your software, but does not prevent structures, components or similar solutions from being reused in other jobs.

external_costs.title: External costs are separate
external_costs.text: VPS, domain and any third-party services are not part of the {price}.

installation.title: Installation
installation.text: If you already have a VPS and need a hand installing the webtool, the installation can be done at no extra cost.

package.label: Illustrative contents of the delivered package

pricing.title: Pricing
pricing.description: The standard price of a webtool is {price}. Complete software, source code and ZIP included, with no recurring fee.
pricing.heading: You pay for the webtool. Not for a subscription.
pricing.lead: The standard price includes the complete software, the source code, the ZIP and the installation instructions. Payment happens only after you have seen and accepted the demo.

after_demo.label: after the demo
after_demo.question: accept?
after_demo.text: If the answer is no, the process ends: you do not pay the {price} and you do not receive the software. If the answer is yes, you pay and receive the complete package.
